# Bundling custom fonts in an Obsidian theme

**Status:** decided 2026-05-19 — base64 data URIs, generated via `build.mjs`
**Date:** 2026-05-19
**Tracks:** issue #15 (Lane 3 → Lane 2 audit packet), Findings 7 + 8

---

## Decision

**Base64 data URIs, embedded in `src:`, generated by a build step.**

`theme.src.css` (hand-authored, Lane 2) keeps readable
`url('fonts/x.woff2')` references. `themes/build.mjs`'s `obsidian-fonts`
pass swaps each for the base64 of the matching woff2 and writes the
distributed `theme.css` (generated, Lane 3). The `fonts/` directory is the
build input / source-of-truth.

Rejected: `local()`-only. It would lock distribution into "install five
fonts manually first" — especially punishing for iA Writer Quattro, which
is not on Google Fonts and ships only from `iaolo/iA-Fonts`. The community
theme value proposition is bundled fonts that work on first load.

---

## The problem

Every `@font-face` in v0.6.0–v0.6.3 used `url('fonts/x.woff2')`. In
Obsidian, **every one of those requests 404s**. Observed in DevTools:

```
GET app://obsidian.md/fonts/jetbrains-mono-400.woff2 net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
GET app://obsidian.md/fonts/ia-writer-quattro-400.woff2 net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
...
```

The files exist on disk at
`<vault>/.obsidian/themes/Artificer/fonts/*.woff2`. The relative URL still
fails, because Obsidian resolves it against the app root
(`app://obsidian.md/`) rather than against `theme.css`'s own location — so
the request lands at a path with nothing behind it.

This was the **upstream cause masking every other font finding** in the
audit. As long as the fonts never loaded, the bundled JetBrains Mono being
a Basic-Latin subset (no box-drawing glyphs) was irrelevant, and the
"true-monospace" tracking reset only operated on whatever OS fallback was
actually rendering. On macOS that fallback is SF Mono, whose box-drawing
glyphs are visibly wider than its ASCII glyphs — the real reason ASCII
diagrams misaligned all along.

## Why relative URLs don't resolve — by design

Obsidian blocks local file access from theme CSS as a mitigation for
**CVE-2023-2110** (a malicious theme could otherwise read arbitrary local
files via CSS `url()`). No URL form resolves:

- `url('fonts/x.woff2')` — resolved against app root, 404
- `url('./fonts/x.woff2')` — same
- `url('file:///…')` — blocked
- `url('app://local/…')` — blocked

The `app://obsidian.md/fonts/x.woff2` 404 is **expected behavior**, not a
bug to work around.

## The two supported patterns

| | Base64 data URIs | `local()` only |
|---|---|---|
| Self-contained | Yes — woff2 bytes live in `theme.css` | No — relies on OS-installed fonts |
| First-load works | Always | Only if the user pre-installed the fonts |
| `theme.css` size | +~700 KB (binary as base64) | Unchanged |
| Diff readability | Destroyed if hand-edited → needs source/artifact split | Fine |
| iA Writer Quattro | Bundled, works everywhere | User must fetch from `iaolo/iA-Fonts` manually |

Base64 is the only method Obsidian's own theme docs document as working
for distributable themes.

## Consequence: the source/artifact split (Finding 8)

Base64-embedding 13 woff2 files (~700 KB) directly into a hand-edited
`theme.css` balloons it from ~80 KB to ~760 KB and buries real CSS changes
under unreviewable blobs. The fix is to separate source from artifact:

- `theme.src.css` — hand-authored, references fonts by `url('fonts/x')`,
  stays ~80 KB and reviewable. **Lane 2 territory.**
- `theme.css` — generated, base64-inlined, carries a do-not-edit banner,
  committed because the Obsidian community picker / BRAT pulls it from the
  repo. **Lane 3 territory.**
- `build.mjs` `obsidian-fonts` pass — reads source + `fonts/`, emits the
  artifact. Same shape as the existing palette → surface passes; only the
  input flavor differs (hand-authored CSS vs. `_palette.json`).

Verification the pass should preserve: non-font CSS is byte-identical
between source and artifact, and the build is deterministic across runs.

## Resurfaced once base64 wins: the JBM subset (Finding 2)

While fonts 404'd, the bundled JetBrains Mono being a 21 KB Basic-Latin
subset (229 glyphs, **zero** box-drawing) was moot. Base64 makes the fonts
actually load — so the subset now matters again: ASCII diagrams will still
misalign because box-drawing glyphs fall back to a different font with
different cell metrics. The full JBM (v2.304) ships 1363 glyphs with
128/128 box-drawing. Swapping the build input to full-unicode JBM
(~90 KB/weight) is the completion of this decision, not a separate one.

```python
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
f = TTFont('JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf')
f.flavor = 'woff2'
f.save('jetbrains-mono-400.woff2')
```

## OS-level install (the `local()` fallback path)

Even on the base64 path, `local()` entries in the `src:` chain let an
OS-installed copy win first (avoids decoding the embedded blob). Install
paths on macOS:

```bash
brew install --cask font-jetbrains-mono-nerd-font
# iA Writer Quattro (OFL) — not on Google Fonts:
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/iaolo/iA-Fonts.git
find iA-Fonts -name "iAWriterQuattro*.ttf" -exec cp {} ~/Library/Fonts/ \;
```

Restart Obsidian after install — fonts aren't picked up live.

## Sources

- Obsidian Help — Theme development / CSS variables (base64 `@font-face`
  is the documented bundling method).
- CVE-2023-2110 — Obsidian local file disclosure via CSS; the mitigation
  that blocks `url()` to local paths in theme CSS.
- `iaolo/iA-Fonts` — OFL-licensed canonical source for iA Writer
  Quattro / Duo / Mono.
- JetBrains Mono v2.304 release — full-unicode TTF with box-drawing
  coverage.
